subject.title: Dead-lettered inbound events are unrecoverable and invisible: payload erased on fail(), re-submissions swallowed, no operator surface (outbound delivery queue has one)

question: Should shared ingress failed rows retain replayable payloads and support operator recovery, or should OpenClaw keep destructive tombstones and only add aggregate observability?
rationale: The requested change affects retained user data, duplicate-delivery safety, and the public operator workflow; the issue deliberately leaves the product surface open.

options.title: Bounded recovery policy
options.body: Retain a protected payload for a short documented TTL, add health/doctor visibility, and provide an explicitly fenced operator replay or supersede path.

options.title: Observability-only policy
options.body: Keep terminal payload erasure and duplicate suppression, but add failed-ingress counts and diagnostics so operators can investigate without replaying content.

options.title: Channel-specific handling
options.body: Keep the core queue generic and require each channel plugin to surface or recover its own failed inbound events.

recommendation.title: Bounded recovery policy
recommendation.body: Retain a protected payload for a short documented TTL, add health/doctor visibility, and provide an explicitly fenced operator replay or supersede path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work adopted the shared ingress drain for LINE and is the strongest supplied ownership signal for the affected queue integration.
